title: Faith and Truth - Episode 5: Anchored in the Promise

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome again to our SleepFit podcast series. This is Faith and Truth - Episode 5: Anchored in the Promise. It is your old friend again, Sarah Mitchell. <short pause> Tonight, I want to ask you something... <short pause> when everything around you is moving, what keeps your faith steady? <long pause>

The letter to the Hebrews was written for people who were tired. <short pause> They'd started out strong... but the road turned out longer than they'd imagined. <short pause> Some were discouraged. Some were quietly doubting. <short pause> Maybe you know that feeling. <long pause>

And the writer doesn't scold them. <short pause> He gives them something to hold. <short pause> God's promise is sure... and not because we're strong. <short pause> Because he is faithful. <long pause>

He reminds them of how God made that promise. <short pause> When we want people to believe us, we say, I swear by something bigger than me. <short pause> But God has nothing bigger to swear by... so he swore by himself. <long pause>
Let that sink in for a moment. <short pause> God put his own name on the line. <long pause>

That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil; <long pause>

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Two things that cannot change. <short pause> A promise... <short pause> and an oath. <short pause> And it is impossible... for God to lie. <long pause>
So the promise doesn't wobble when your feelings do. <short pause> It doesn't fade when your circumstances turn. <short pause> God simply cannot go back on his word. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: And I know what you might be thinking, lying here in the dark. <short pause> That's lovely... but what does it do for me, tonight? <long pause>
Here's what it does. <short pause> It turns hope into something solid. <short pause> This kind of hope isn't a wish. <short pause> It's an anchor. <long pause>

Picture a ship out on open water. <short pause> The wind rises, the waves lift it and drop it... and on the surface, everything is moving. <short pause> But far below, out of sight, the anchor has taken hold. <short pause> And the ship... stays. <long pause>

That's what the promise of God is for your soul. <short pause> Your anchor isn't your own strength. It isn't how well you understand things. <short pause> It's set in something far deeper. <long pause>

The Scripture says this hope reaches all the way behind the veil... into the very presence of God. <short pause> And Jesus is already there. <short pause> He went ahead of us, as our forerunner... to hold the other end of the line. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So when the wind blows in your life, and it will... you are held. <short pause> When the doubts come, and they do... you are anchored. <short pause> Not because you feel strong. <short pause> Because the promise is sure. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: The writer calls this a strong consolation. <short pause> A comfort that does more than soothe... it steadies you. It settles the soul. <short pause> And he says it's for those who have fled for refuge. <long pause>

Think of someone running in from a storm, looking for shelter. <short pause> If you've turned to Christ... that's you. <short pause> You've already run to the refuge. <short pause> And the refuge isn't a feeling. <short pause> It's a person... and a promise that will not fail. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: There's real rest in that. <short pause> Your hope doesn't depend on how well you hold on. <short pause> You're not hanging by your fingernails. <short pause> You're anchored. <long pause>
And the anchor holds for one simple reason. <short pause> It's fixed in the character of God... and God does not change. <short pause> The prophet Malachi puts it this way. <long pause>
For I am the Lord, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed. <long pause>
He doesn't change. <short pause> What he promised yesterday... he promises today... and he'll promise again tomorrow. <long pause>
So what do you do on a night when your faith feels small? <long pause>

You remember that faith isn't a feeling. <short pause> It's trusting someone who has already proven faithful. <short pause> You remember that the anchor isn't in your grip... it's in his. <short pause> And you remember that he swore by himself... and he cannot lie. <long pause>

That's how we take hold of the hope in front of us. <short pause> Not by working up a feeling... but by resting in what's been promised. <short pause> The hope is already there. It's real. It's sure. <short pause> All we do is reach for it... like a tired traveler reaching for a railing. <long pause>

And can I point out the kindness in this? <short pause> God knows we're weak. He knows how easily we doubt. <short pause> So he didn't give us only a promise. He gave us an oath. <short pause> His own name... as the guarantee. <short pause> He made it as certain as he possibly could, because he loves us... and he knows what we need. <long pause>
One more passage, before we rest. <short pause> It comes from Paul. <long pause>

For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. <long pause>

Nothing. <short pause> Not even your doubt. <short pause> Not your weariness. <short pause> Not your fear. <short pause> Nothing can separate you from the love of God. <short pause> The anchor holds. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: <exhales> So tonight, as your body settles... let your soul settle too. <short pause> You don't have to hold everything together. <short pause> You are held. <short pause> The God who cannot lie has given you his word... and that word is an anchor, sure and steadfast, reaching into his very presence. <long pause>
Let's pray. <long pause> Father, thank you that your promise is sure... even when our faith feels small. <short pause> Anchor our souls tonight... in the hope we find in you alone. <long pause>
Rest well, friend. <short pause> Goodnight.
